author: TEDx Talks
description: For 70 years after Sputnik, space launches happened slowly and infrequently. Today, something launches into space almost every single day. That acceleration raises a new question: what happens to the human body during extended space travel? The NASA Twin Study, which observed Scott Kelly in space for a year while his brother Mark remained on Earth, produced the first complete molecular map of the changes the human body undergoes in space. That data is now informing a new generation of research into the cell engineering needed to make humans self-sufficient for long-duration missions. Gene-editing therapies that once seemed hypothetical have already moved from clinical trials to FDA approval in under three years, blurring the boundary between science fiction and reality.  Christopher Mason is the WorldQuant Professor of Genomics and Computational Biomedicine at Weill Cornell Medicine, where he directs the Mason Lab and the Cornell Aerospace Medicine Biobank. He holds a dual BS in genet
title: How to engineer humans for life beyond Earth | Christopher Mason | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are living in an age where our minds are more powerful than ever — constantly thinking, creating, imagining, and processing at incredible speed. But if our potential is so vast, why do we still feel stuck?

In this engaging and relatable talk at TEDxBITJaipur, Gaurav Juyal uses a powerful metaphor — a rocket brain with bicycle brakes — to describe the gap between our capabilities and our actions. While our minds are capable of extraordinary ideas, our fears, doubts, habits, and conditioning often slow us down.

We overthink instead of acting. We hesitate instead of trying. We limit ourselves not because we lack ability, but because we lack alignment between our thoughts and our execution.

Through simple yet impactful insights, Gaurav highlights how internal barriers — fear of failure, overanalysis, and self-doubt — act like brakes on a system designed to soar. The real challenge is not building a stronger mind, but learning how to release these brakes.

This talk is a wake-up call
title: A Rocket Brain with Bicycle Brakes | Gaurav Juyal | TEDxBIT Jaipur

Friendships are amazing but can become messy or dramatic. In this talk, Andrew sheds light on what friendship really means and how we can strengthen our connections with friends. Going through university is about building new friendships - but what about old ones? Old connections cannot be dismissed.

"Let's be friends." Just a three-word sentence from one seemingly ordinary assembly talk during secondary school still lingers in me. What can be start of a friendship can evolve into dynamic social circles, networks and relationships. Once playing with friends on an online game every Friday, chilling after a toiling school week, is now once a blue moon as your friends scatter.

Everyone goes through a friendship change - or should I say the three phases of friendships: fully connect, gracefully disconnect, friendships will stick around. title: The cyclical nature of friendship | Andrew Maghari | TEDxUoN

description: In his speech, Parth looks at the other side of the coin of failure. Rather than as a setback or scar, he shows how disappointment can serve as essential data, motivation, and fuel, turning life’s hardest moments into catalysts for growth through resilience. Along the way, he uses powerful, active examples from his own life to show how he’s changed because of all his failures.  Failure is universal, but it is not the end. I reframe failure as data, motivation, and resilience, showing how setbacks can be weaponised to drive growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Weaponizing Failure | Parth Karnik | TEDxWinchesterSchoolJebelAli

description:
Işıl Tabağ, konuşmasına doğum hikâyesiyle başlıyor. İzmir’de dünyaya geldiği gün hastanede askeri harekât nedeniyle olan karartmanın kaldırıldığını ve bir anda her yerin aydınlandığını anlatıyor. Ailesi bu nedenle ona “Işıl” adını veriyor. Tabağ bu hikâyeyi, hayatın en karanlık anlarında bile küçük bir ışığın yol gösterebileceğinin sembolü olarak görüyor.
Yıllar sonra anne olmak istediğinde, hamile kalmasının çok zor olabileceğini öğrendiğinde, bunun kendisinde eksiklik duygusu yarattığını hissediyor. Ancak zamanla bunun aslında toplumun insanlara yapıştırdığı bir etiket olduğunu fark ediyor.
Bu süreçte psikolog Carol Dweck’in “henüz” kavramıyla tanışması bakış açısını değiştiriyor.
“ ‘Başaramıyorum.’ demek yerine ‘Henüz başaramıyorum.’ demek umudu canlı tutar.”

description: People support what they help create. It sounds simple, but most leaders spend their careers doing the opposite - crafting the perfect plan and wondering why their teams won't fully commit to it. This talk is about what changes when you stop selling your vision and start co-creating it instead. Dr Patrick Farran is a leadership researcher, educator, and organisational strategist based in the midwest, US. With a background spanning business leadership, organisational behaviour, and team performance, Patrick studies how leaders inspire commitment and alignment in complex organisations. His work focuses on trust, shared purpose, and co-creation as drivers of sustainable leadership. Drawing on academic research and real-world experience, Patrick challenges traditional top-down leadership models and offers a human-centred approach to building teams that genuinely believe in the future they are creating together. author: TEDx Talks
description:
La charla de Yuyita de Chiossone se despliega como un puente de sabiduría entre dos siglos, donde la elegancia del piano se funde con la firmeza del servicio público.

A sus casi 83 años, la ponente nos regala una crónica de vanguardia y entrega, rememorando una época en la que el destino de la mujer parecía confinado a los muros del hogar.

Con una voz que resuena con la autoridad de la experiencia, Yuyita narra cómo desafió los moldes de su tiempo para convertirse en la arquitecta de la institucionalidad musical de Barquisimeto.

La charla describe su ascenso desde las teclas del piano hasta la dirección del primer conservatorio de la ciudad ante el Ministerio de Educación de Venezuela. 

Sin embargo, la charla revela que su liderazgo no se detuvo en las artes; se expandió hacia el servicio al Estado como Secretaria de Gobierno y Directora de Educación.

A través de este relato, Yuyita siembra una premisa que sacude las nociones modernas de autorrealización: el objeto de la vida es
title: El servicio como brújula de la vida  | Yuyita Ríos de Chiossone | TEDxSanta Rosa Women
